domain: Islamic Jurisprudence / Legal Theory / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the four Sunni schools of jurisprudence (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) as a contested kernel system. Each school offers a distinct reading of the shared jurisprudential-method kernel (usul al-fiqh), grounding interpretive authority differently while maintaining mutual recognition. The system exhibits stable pluralism across 1200+ years without displacement or convergence.

key_entities: Hanafi school (founded Abu Hanifa, 8th century; emphasizes qiyas/analogical reasoning, ra'y/opinion)
Maliki school (founded Malik ibn Anas; emphasizes Medinan practice, maslaha/public interest)
Shafi'i school (founded al-Shafi'i; systematized usul al-fiqh, hierarchical source methodology)
Hanbali school (founded Ahmad ibn Hanbal; textualist, restricts qiyas, emphasizes hadith)
Usul al-fiqh (shared jurisprudential-method kernel: Quran, Sunnah, ijma, qiyas as source hierarchy)
Taqlid (following established school authority vs independent reasoning)
Ikhtilaf (jurisprudential disagreement; recognized as legitimate diversity)
key_tensions: Textualist restriction (Hanbali) vs expansive analogical reasoning (Hanafi)
Medinan practice as binding precedent (Maliki) vs systematic hadith hierarchy (Shafi'i)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Usul al-fiqh: the shared jurisprudential-method framework identifying Quran, Sunnah, ijma (consensus), and qiyas (analogy) as legitimate sources of legal derivation
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Each school grounds interpretive legitimacy in its founder's methodological commitments and transmitted chain of scholarly authority (isnad), not in institutional hierarchy or democratic mandate

readings.commitment: Expansive qiyas and ra'y (juristic preference) as necessary tools for legal derivation when texts are silent or ambiguous
readings.authority_grounding: Abu Hanifa's rationalist methodology; transmitted through Iraqi scholarly lineage; institutional dominance in Ottoman/Mughal empires
readings.expected_structural_delta: Lowest textual constraint (high epsilon for analogical extension); beneficiary: jurists with discretion; victim: textualist certainty

readings.commitment: Medinan practice ('amal ahl al-Madina) as authoritative interpretive layer over hadith; maslaha (public interest) as legitimate source
readings.authority_grounding: Malik's proximity to Prophetic community; transmitted through North African/Andalusian scholarly networks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Practice-norm constraint over textual hierarchy; beneficiary: local custom preservation; victim: universal textualist uniformity

readings.commitment: Systematic hierarchical source methodology: Quran > Sunnah > ijma > qiyas, with strict conditions on each level
readings.authority_grounding: Al-Shafi'i's Risala as founding text of usul al-fiqh; transmitted through Egyptian/Levantine scholarly institutions
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate constraint via procedural hierarchy; beneficiary: methodological systematizers; victim: both expansive qiyas and pure textualism

readings.commitment: Textualist restriction: minimize qiyas, prioritize hadith over juristic reasoning, reject speculative methods
readings.authority_grounding: Ahmad ibn Hanbal's hadith-centered methodology; transmitted through Syrian/Najdi scholarly networks; Salafi revival movements
readings.expected_structural_delta: Highest textual constraint (low epsilon for extension); beneficiary: hadith scholars; victim: contextual adaptation capacity

axes.structural_delta: Qiyas and ra'y as necessary juristic tools when texts are silent or ambiguous
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of qiyas deployment in fatawa; acceptance of juristic preference (istihsan) in rulings
axes.selection_reason: Highest epsilon reading; represents one pole of the textualist-rationalist spectrum

axes.human_readable: Maliki Reading (Medinan Practice as Authoritative Layer)
axes.structural_delta: Local practice-norm ('amal) as interpretive constraint over textual hierarchy
axes.primary_observable: Invocation of Medinan practice in fatawa; maslaha-based rulings vs strict hadith application
axes.selection_reason: Structurally distinct from Hanafi (practice vs reason) and Hanbali (custom vs text); moderate epsilon

axes.structural_delta: Minimize qiyas, prioritize hadith, reject speculative juristic methods
axes.primary_observable: Restriction of qiyas deployment; hadith citation density in fatawa vs juristic reasoning
axes.selection_reason: Opposite pole from Hanafi; lowest epsilon reading; completes the structural spectrum

axes.structural_delta: Procedural hierarchy (Quran > Sunnah > ijma > qiyas) with strict conditions at each level
axes.primary_observable: Adherence to four-source hierarchy in fatawa; rejection of both expansive qiyas and pure textualism
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: structurally intermediate between Hanafi and Hanbali; lower distinctiveness within three-axis budget

axes.structural_delta: Obligation to follow one school's rulings vs freedom to select across schools (talfiq)
axes.primary_observable: Institutional enforcement of school loyalty; prevalence of cross-school fatwa shopping
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream enforcement mechanism rather than kernel reading; captured in omega_taqlid_enforcement

axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream enabling condition rather than kernel reading; captured in omega_pluralism_stability

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Structurally intermediate between Hanafi and Hanbali poles; lower distinctiveness within three-reading budget

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Disagreement recognized as legitimate diversity rather than error
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream enabling condition for pluralism stability; not a kernel reading itself

omegas.description: Why does this system exhibit 1200+ years of stable pluralism without displacement or convergence? Is ikhtilaf_legitimacy a true Mountain (theological necessity) or a Rope (coordination equilibrium that could collapse)? Salafi movements test this boundary.
omegas.source: Deferred axis ikhtilaf_legitimacy + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Does taqlid (school loyalty) function as a Rope (voluntary coordination) or Snare (institutional extraction via monopoly on interpretation)? Modern fatwa-shopping and online eclecticism test enforcement capacity.
omegas.source: Deferred axis taqlid_constraint + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Does state adoption of one school (Ottoman Hanafi, Saudi Hanbali) convert that reading from Tangled Rope to Snare via enforcement apparatus? Post-colonial legal pluralism may reveal extraction structure.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — analysis conducted within assumption of non-state enforcement

omegas.description: Is Shafi'i reading's procedural systematization the hidden structural center (highest actual centrality) that enables the other three to coexist? Deferral may have excluded the load-bearing axis.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel recognition confirmed: four readings emit structurally different constraints (different epsilon bins, different beneficiary/victim pairs, different authority-grounding). Shafi'i deferral is structural budget constraint, not analytical error. Omega_shafii_centrality bounds the selection uncertainty.
